briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Tensions in the Middle East remain extremely high, characterized by conflicting signals between Iran and the United States regarding potential negotiations and the ongoing militarization of the Strait of Hormuz. Israel continues to conduct targeted military operations in Gaza and Lebanon, while facing internal political turmoil related to defense policy and religious conscription.

IRAN
Iran reports significant internal security incidents, with two Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) servicemen martyred in a "terror attack" in Paveh, Kermanshah province, on 29 June. Another senior IRGC Navy official, Mohammad Akbar-zadeh, described as a "mastermind" behind Iran's Strait of Hormuz strategy, was reported killed in a traffic accident in Kerman on 29 June, though some sources imply it was suspicious. A "US-Israeli-linked terrorist group" is blamed for an attack in Saravan, southeastern Iran, which killed a driver and wounded his wife and child.

Diplomatically, Iran's Foreign Ministry Spokesman stated that no direct high-level negotiations with the US are planned, contradicting US President Trump's claim that Iran requested a meeting in Doha. However, Iran confirmed a technical delegation is traveling to Doha to discuss the implementation of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MOU), including the release of frozen assets. Qatar's Foreign Ministry confirmed that $6 billion of Iranian funds remain frozen. President Pezeshkian stated that Iran will fulfill its commitments if the US adheres to the agreement.

The management and security of the Strait of Hormuz remains a critical issue. Iran's Acting Defense Minister reiterated that "the finger remains on the trigger" and Tehran is ready to respond to any ceasefire breach, asserting Iran's sole responsibility for demining and management of the Strait. Oman's Foreign Minister expressed support for Iran's plan to impose "maritime service fees" but also stressed international commitments to free passage.

Internal Iranian affairs are dominated by preparations for the funeral of the "martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution," with ceremonies planned in Tehran, Qom, and Iraq from 3-9 July. It was reported that the arrangements are being made with the discretion of the esteemed office and the "new Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei." Over 30 countries and 90 religious leaders are expected to attend.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations continue in the Gaza Strip and southern Lebanon. The IDF and Shin Bet announced the killing of Talal al-Aal, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) commander involved in holding hostages and commanding operatives during the 7 October 2023 attacks. Ismail Masri, Hamas's "military security" chief in the Rafah Brigade, was also killed in an Israeli strike in Gaza last week. The IDF struck a Hamas tunnel system in central Gaza (Deir al-Balah) which Hamas was reportedly attempting to restore in violation of the ceasefire. A massive Hamas tunnel system, over 16 kilometers long with 80 rooms, used to hold the remains of Lt. Hadar Goldin in southern Rafah, was sealed by combat engineers after 18 months of scanning and three months of concrete-filling work.

An IDF reservist was severely wounded by an explosion in Arnoun, southern Lebanon, during operations of the Commando Brigade. The cause of the explosion is under investigation.

Politically, Defense Minister Israel Katz stated that Israel has "no territorial ambitions in Lebanon" but will not withdraw "a millimeter" until Hezbollah is disarmed. He claimed that US pressure under President Trump prevented a "massive" aerial campaign that "would have dismantled Hezbollah" due to the US linking the Lebanon and Iran arenas. Katz also warned that if Iran attacks Israel, the IDF is prepared for an independent "Blue and White" operation, potentially within two days.

Domestic political tensions are high following severe incitement against the IDF Chief of Staff at a Haredi protest in Bnei Brak, condemned by Prime Minister Netanyahu, President Herzog, Benny Gantz, and Yair Lapid. A bill to prevent Red Cross visits to security prisoners (including 7 October operatives) failed in the Knesset due to a boycott by Haredi parties. A Basic Law on Torah Study was approved by a Knesset committee and is slated for a first reading.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli military operations targeted Hamas and PIJ figures and infrastructure. A Palestinian child and her mother were reported killed in an Israeli raid on Gaza. Separately, a young Palestinian girl was martyred after Israeli warplanes bombed tents in Khan Younis, and at least three Palestinians, including a child, were killed in Deir al-Balah.

A Hamas delegation led by Zahar Jabareen is in Cairo to discuss the implementation of the ceasefire agreement, focusing on ending attacks, ensuring full provision of needs, and a roadmap for the second phase, including the deployment of international protection forces and Israeli withdrawal. Despite the ceasefire, the IDF claims Hamas was attempting to restore a tunnel system in Deir al-Balah.

LEBANON
An IDF reservist was severely wounded by an explosion in Arnoun, southern Lebanon. Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz affirmed that Israel has no territorial ambitions in Lebanon but will not withdraw until Hezbollah is disarmed, citing 100% destruction in western and central sectors and 73% in the eastern sector of southern Lebanese villages along the line of contact. Katz stated that 600,000 Shiites from southern Lebanon and 700,000 from Beirut's Dahiyeh stronghold have been displaced. US Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper met with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun following the Israel-Lebanon agreement. A US official indicated that the US role in the region includes the use of American forces on the ground in Lebanon and Israel.

SYRIA & IRAQ
An IDF soldier's cellphone was found dropped in Tal al-Maghar hill, near the border village of Abidin, southern Syria, with the incident under review by the IDF. In Syria, "Gulani gangs" (likely Hayat Tahrir al-Sham) were reported to be demolishing Shiite homes in Al-Mazraa village, Homs, and arresting women in an alleged attempt at forced displacement.

In Iraq, Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi stated that Iraq will not allow its territory to be used for attacks on neighboring countries. An explosion was reported in Maysan province, southern Iraq, and Iraqi counter-terrorism forces arrested a government official in Erbil. Iraqi judiciary issued prison sentences for three Diwaniya province officials for embezzling funds meant for martyrs' and wounded persons' compensation. Iraq's PM announced the full withdrawal of Coalition forces by 30 September. Drone flights were reported over Baghdad. Iraq's Foreign Minister discussed an oil pipeline with the Syrian President.

GULF STATES
Qatar continues its role as a key intermediary, hosting US envoys Witkoff and Kushner for discussions with Qatari and Pakistani intermediaries regarding the US-Iran MOU, though Qatar's Foreign Ministry explicitly stated no direct high-level meetings between US and Iranian officials are scheduled. Qatar also issued an advisory for all maritime vessels to temporarily suspend sailing and other maritime activities until further notice, for public safety.

Oman's Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaidi reportedly expressed support for Iran's plan to impose "maritime service fees" on vessels crossing the Strait of Hormuz, while also stressing Oman's commitment to international law for free passage without transit fees, and affirming Iran's primary responsibility for demining the Strait. The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs lifted its travel ban to Lebanon as of 29 June 2026. Pakistan's Interior Minister visited Saudi Arabia for security coordination talks.

Two US aircraft carriers remain deployed near Iran, with no immediate plans to leave the region. Oil prices decreased, possibly due to a perceived easing of tensions following the Iran-US MOU.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1. **US-Iran Diplomatic Chess:** US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are in Doha for talks with Qatari intermediaries regarding the Iran MOU. Iran confirms a technical delegation will attend but denies any direct, high-level meetings with US officials.
2. **Iran's Strategic Strait of Hormuz Stance:** Iran's Acting Defense Minister stated "finger remains on trigger," threatening response to ceasefire breaches, and asserted Iran's sole responsibility for demining and management of the Strait, including imposing "maritime service fees."
3. **Internal Security Incidents in Iran:** Two IRGC servicemen were martyred in a "terror attack" in Paveh, Kermanshah. Separately, Mohammad Akbar-zadeh, a senior IRGC Navy official, died in a "traffic accident" in Kerman, with some speculation about the circumstances.
4. **Targeted Killings in Gaza:** The IDF and Shin Bet killed Talal al-Aal, a PIJ commander involved in holding hostages, and Ismail Masri, Hamas's military security chief in Rafah.
5. **Gaza Tunnel System Neutralized:** The IDF sealed a massive 16-kilometer Hamas tunnel system in southern Rafah that held the remains of Lt. Hadar Goldin, using over 30,000 cubic meters of concrete.
6. **Israel's Tough Stance on Lebanon:** Defense Minister Israel Katz announced Israel will not withdraw "a millimeter" from Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed and claimed US pressure prevented a full IDF campaign to dismantle Hezbollah in the past.
7. **Qatar's Maritime Warning:** The Qatari Ministry of Transportation advised all maritime vessels to temporarily suspend sailing and other maritime activities until further notice, citing public safety.
8. **New Iranian Leadership Indication:** Shargh Daily reported funeral preparations for the "martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution" and mentioned arrangements were made under the guidance of the "new Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei."

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain extremely high across multiple fronts. In the Iran-Israel context, Defense Minister Katz's statements about preparing for a potential "Blue and White" operation against Iran, and Iran's Acting Defense Minister's "finger on the trigger" warning, indicate an acute risk of direct military confrontation. The Strait of Hormuz is an active flashpoint, with conflicting interpretations of international law and potential for maritime incidents, underscored by Qatar's recent advisory. The Israel-Lebanon border remains volatile, with an IDF reservist severely wounded and Israel's explicit refusal to withdraw until Hezbollah is disarmed. Inside Iran, the reported "terror attacks" in Kermanshah and Saravan, combined with the suspicious death of a senior IRGC official, point to ongoing internal instability or covert operations. Militias in Syria and Iraq also continue to operate, with the Iraqi PM's warning against using Iraqi soil to attack neighbors highlighting regional spillover concerns. US officials mentioning the use of American forces on the ground in Lebanon and Israel adds another layer of complexity and potential for broader engagement.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** posture is characterized by a mix of diplomatic outreach and military presence. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are engaged in indirect talks with Iran via Qatari and Pakistani intermediaries in Doha. US Central Command chief Adm. Brad Cooper met with Lebanese President Joseph Aoun. Two US aircraft carriers remain in the region near Iran. US President Trump's various statements and SCOTUS rulings impacting his legal appeals reflect internal political dynamics.

Among **Gulf States**, Qatar is actively facilitating US-Iran talks while issuing a temporary maritime activity suspension. Oman has supported Iran's stance on "maritime service fees" in Hormuz but also reaffirmed commitment to free passage. The UAE lifted its travel ban to Lebanon.

**EU members** include the European Commission advancing a loan to Ukraine. France's Foreign Minister discussed the Islamabad MoU with Iran. The UK's Defense Minister pledged to strengthen nuclear deterrence.

Russia reported intercepting 419 Ukrainian drones. China and the EU launched new "Trade and Investment Consultations" to address trade deficits. Turkey's Defense Minister confirmed the US has no intention of leaving NATO.

Other notable responses include Spain's Prime Minister announcing the regularization of over one million illegal immigrants, and UN preparations for a potentially high death toll from earthquakes in Venezuela.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
There are significant contradictions regarding US-Iran direct talks in Doha. US President Trump claimed Iran requested a meeting for 30 June in Doha, which was immediately contradicted by Iran's Foreign Ministry Spokesman, who stated no direct high-level meetings are planned. Qatari officials also confirmed US envoys would meet with intermediaries, not directly with Iranians. This highlights a deliberate ambiguity or divergence in communication strategies.

A highly sensitive and potentially unverified claim from Shargh Daily mentions the passing of the "Leader of the Islamic Revolution" (Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei) and explicitly names "Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei" as the "new Leader of the Islamic Revolution" in the context of funeral preparations. This is a monumental development if true, but appears in a single Iranian source within the raw feed and is not explicitly confirmed by other Iranian state media (Press TV refers to "martyred Leader" without explicitly stating the passing of the current Supreme Leader, or the succession). This requires immediate and high-priority verification.

The death of Mohammad Akbar-zadeh, a senior IRGC Navy official, in a "traffic accident" in Kerman is also reported by Iranian sources, with some internal Iranian commentary (from Omid Dana) suggesting it was a "mysterious and very strange" incident, implying foul play. This remains unverified.

Propaganda indicators are present in Iranian state media, such as the "Hamshahri" newspaper cover depicting Trump with a rifle scope and the text "Revenge is inevitable," and claims that a recent terror attack in Saravan was carried out by a "US-Israeli-linked terrorist group." Hamas's statement that global silence on Palestinian children's deaths constitutes complicity in genocide is also a clear propaganda narrative.

Reporting gaps include the precise nature of recent Hezbollah operations in Lebanon and the specific mandate for the "use of US forces on the ground" in Lebanon and Israel as mentioned by a US official.
